clue.text: Drink making one complain audibly

indicators.note: audibly asks for the word as heard spoken rather than as written

parts.note: to whine is what someone does when they complain in a nagging voice

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drink and promptly starts grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: WHINE and WINE are said the same way in most accents, so the spoken complaint gives the written drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermented grape juice is a standard example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Panelling I now cast out

indicators.note: out in its sense of disordered or wrong tells us these letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A craftsman announces he is throwing away some wooden panelling.
explanation.definitionFit: It is wooden panelling lining the lower part of a room's walls.

clue.text: Short statement made by school after upset

indicators.note: after being upset, turned over, in a down clue the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school issues a brief statement following some disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief written message or remark is a synonym for a short statement.

clue.text: East Anglian town with ten involved in protest

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, in East Anglia in eastern England

indicators.note: involved in its sense of tangled or twisted signals that the three letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: People in a small Norfolk town, ten of them, join a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' gives ENT. Diss is a small Norfolk town that few solvers outside Britain will know; 'protest' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent is disagreement voiced openly, which is what a protest expresses; the noun senses are synonyms.

clue.text: Ornamentation I'd made specially

indicators.note: specially as in made to a special design suggests the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a decorative piece they made specially.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled headband or crown worn as an ornament is a form of ornamentation.

clue.text: Her (Peep's) dish possibly?

parts.note: Little Bo Peep is the shepherdess of the nursery rhyme, so a dish she owned could be named for a sheep-keeper

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which plate of food belongs to a nursery-rhyme girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Bo Peep, of the nursery rhyme, lost her sheep. The British dish is minced lamb topped with mashed potato.
explanation.definitionFit: The baked minced-lamb-and-mash dish is read as the meal belonging to a female sheep-keeper.

clue.text: One may be lacking in spirit after my visit

definitions.text: One may be lacking in spirit after my visit

parts.words: One may be lacking in spirit after my visit
parts.note: the visitor drives out an evil spirit, leaving the possessed person without one

explanation.surface: A boastful guest who leaves people feeling deflated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking in spirit' suggests low morale, but here it means freed of a possessing demon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric who expels demons leaves the possessed person literally without a spirit inside them.

clue.text: Monkey — it climbs repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly says the reversed pair appears twice in a row
climbs in a down clue means the word goes upward, so it reads bottom to top

explanation.surface: A monkey keeps scrambling up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The titi is a small South American monkey, a specific example.

clue.text: With characters dispersing, distant noise ends for traveller

indicators.note: the characters, meaning letters, are scattered and so reassemble in another order

explanation.surface: As people scatter, a faraway noise fades out for a wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' is a noun, the goals of a journey, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The places a traveller is heading for are the end points of each trip.

clue.text: Oxford and Cambridge crews will not be suffering similarly

definitions.text: Oxford and Cambridge crews will not be
definitions.meaning: in the Boat Race each university rows its own boat, so the two crews are never sharing one vessel
an idiom for sharing the same difficult situation as someone else

explanation.surface: A remark about the Boat Race rivals, who cannot both be having the same bad time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing race on the Thames; the literal reading of the idiom is what the crews avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes people facing the same predicament, everyone affected alike by the trouble.

clue.text: Part of formal wear as an obligation

definitions.meaning: a neckpiece such as a bow worn with evening dress
something that binds you, like a duty or commitment

explanation.surface: Someone treats dressing up as a duty rather than a pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie in the sense of a bond or commitment restricts freedom, as a duty does.

clue.text: Gosh soldier gets a dog!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, much like gosh
GI is the familiar term for an American private soldier

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight as a serviceman is given a pet dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed of dog, famously kept by Queen Elizabeth II.

clue.text: Bowler approaching the wicket maybe is second-best performer

definitions.meaning: in cricket the bowler runs up to the wicket before delivering, so is one who runs up

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler on his run-up turns out to be only the second-best player.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler runs in towards the stumps, the wicket, before delivering the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitor who finishes second in a contest is the standard sense of the hyphenated term.

clue.text: Satisfying encounter

definitions.meaning: ... a need or demand means satisfying it
a coming together of people, by chance or arrangement

explanation.surface: A pleasing get-together, the kind that leaves both parties content.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a gathering or chance coming together, a synonym for an encounter.

clue.text: Body of soldiers in Saigon wickedly imprisoning bishop

indicators.note: imprisoning means one piece holds the other inside it
wickedly suggests twisted behaviour, so the city's letters are mixed up

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title abbreviation for a bishop

explanation.surface: Troops in wartime Saigon cruelly lock up a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wickedly' gives GAISON, which 'imprisoning' wraps round the bishop: Right Reverend is a bishop's formal title.
explanation.definitionFit: A force of troops stationed to defend a town or fort is a body of soldiers.

clue.text: Sort of tax on agent abroad

indicators.note: abroad in its old sense of widely scattered tells us to spread these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A kind of levy imposed on someone working for you overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a duty charged on ships by their cargo capacity, it is a levy of that particular kind.

clue.text: Infuriate someone finally, with anger stirred up

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it
stirred up, like a mixture, tells us to jumble these letters

explanation.surface: Someone at last loses their temper, worked into a fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone furious is a direct synonym of driving them to fury.

clue.text: Some bride terrified, put off

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nervous bride, scared enough to postpone the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone from acting is a direct synonym of putting them off.

clue.text: Greek characters in student organisation

definitions.meaning: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and these are more than one of it
the National Union of Students, the UK students' body

explanation.surface: Greek letters appear in the name of a student society, as with American fraternities.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the plural of a Greek letter; the other is the initials of the British students' union.

clue.text: Incentive needed with Tottenham team falling short

indicators.note: falling short means the word stops before its final letter

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club

explanation.surface: A struggling Tottenham side needs some motivation.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur, a north London football club, are known as Spurs.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is a stimulus to action, from the rider's goad, so a synonym of incentive.

clue.text: Choose something to break up ground

definitions.meaning: to select, as in to ... a team
a pointed digging tool, a pickaxe

explanation.surface: Instructions to select a tool for digging.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb to select; the other is the pointed tool for loosening hard earth.

clue.text: A-list pioneers, exceptionally distinctive folk

indicators.note: exceptionally hints at something out of the ordinary, so these letters leave their normal order

explanation.surface: Top-ranking trailblazers are, unusually, people who stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrities or people with striking characters are often called personalities, notable individuals in the public eye.

clue.text: In despair I posted sprited reply

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone in low spirits sends off a sharp written retort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprited' is the printed spelling of spirited.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick, sharp retort is exactly a spirited reply, from the fencing term for a counter-thrust.

clue.text: Hide, being endlessly broke

indicators.note: endlessly says the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money

explanation.surface: Someone goes into hiding because they are permanently out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but is the noun, an animal's pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hide is its pelt, the outer covering of its body.
